text: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man! Thus saith Jehovah the God of Israel: I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

title: II Samuel 12:8
text: and I gave thee thy master's house, and thy master's wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if [that] had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.

title: II Samuel 12:9
text: Wherefore hast thou despised the word of Jehovah to do evil in his sight? thou hast smitten Urijah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

title: II Samuel 12:10
text: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thy house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Urijah the Hittite to be thy wife.

title: II Samuel 12:11
text: Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.

title: II Samuel 12:12
text: For thou didst [it] secretly; but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.

title: II Samuel 12:13
text: And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against Jehovah. And Nathan said to David, Jehovah has also put away thy sin: thou shalt not die.

title: II Samuel 12:14
text: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of Jehovah to blaspheme, even the child that is born to thee shall certainly die.

title: II Samuel 12:15
text: ¶And Nathan departed to his house. And Jehovah smote the child that Urijah's wife bore to David, and it became very sick.

title: II Samuel 12:16
text: And David besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night on the earth.

title: II Samuel 12:17
text: And the elders of his house arose, [and went] to him, to raise him up from the earth; but he would not, and he ate no bread with them.

title: II Samuel 12:18
text: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him, and he would not hearken to our voice; and how shall we say to him, The child is dead? he may do some harm.

title: II Samuel 12:19
text: But David saw that his servants whispered, and David perceived that the child was dead; and David said to his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

title: II Samuel 12:20
text: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his clothing, and entered into the house of Jehovah and worshipped; then he came to his own house and required them to set bread before him, and he ate.

title: II Samuel 12:21
text: And his servants said to him, What thing is this which thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child alive; but as soon as the child is dead, thou dost rise and eat bread.

title: II Samuel 12:22
text: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I thought, Who knows? [perhaps] Jehovah will be gracious to me, that the child may live.

title: II Samuel 12:23
text: But now he is dead, why should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me.

title: II Samuel 12:24
text: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and lay with her; and she bore a son, and he called his name Solomon; and Jehovah loved him.

title: II Samuel 12:25
text: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, for Jehovah's sake.

title: II Samuel 12:26
text: ¶And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

title: II Samuel 12:27
text: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.

title: II Samuel 12:28
text: And now gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city and take it: lest I take the city and it be called by my name.

title: II Samuel 12:29
text: And David gathered all the people, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and took it.

title: II Samuel 12:30
text: And he took the crown of their king from off his head, the weight of which was a talent of gold with [the] precious stones; and it was [set] on David's head; and he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.

title: II Samuel 12:31
text: And he brought out the people that were in it, and put them under the saw, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkilns. And so did he to all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 13:1
text: ¶And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David having a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar, Amnon the son of David loved her.

title: II Samuel 13:2
text: And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed difficult for Amnon to do the least thing to her.

title: II Samuel 13:3
text: And Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.

title: II Samuel 13:4
text: And he said to him, Why dost thou, the king's son, get thinner from morning to morning? Wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.

title: II Samuel 13:5
text: And Jonadab said to him, Lay thee down on thy bed and feign thyself sick; and when thy father comes to see thee, say to him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me food, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.

title: II Samuel 13:6
text: So Amnon lay down and feigned himself sick; and the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.

title: II Samuel 13:7
text: And David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go, I pray thee, to thy brother Amnon's house, and dress him food.

title: II Samuel 13:8
text: And Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house; and he had lain down. And she took flour and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.

title: II Samuel 13:9
text: And she took the pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Put every man out from me. And they went out every man from him.

title: II Samuel 13:10
text: And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the dish into the chamber, that I may eat of thy hand. And Tamar took the cakes that she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.

title: II Samuel 13:11
text: And she presented them to him to eat; and he took hold of her, and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister.

title: II Samuel 13:12
text: And she said to him, No, my brother, do not humble me; for no such thing is done in Israel: do not this infamy.

title: II Samuel 13:13
text: And I, whither shall I carry my reproach? and thou wouldest be as one of the infamous in Israel. And now, I pray thee, speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.

title: II Samuel 13:14
text: But he would not hearken to her voice, and was stronger than she, and humbled her and lay with her.

title: II Samuel 13:15
text: And Amnon hated her with an exceeding great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, Arise, be gone.

title: II Samuel 13:16
text: And she said to him, There is no cause for this evil in sending me away, [which] is greater than the other that thou didst to me. But he would not hearken to her.

title: II Samuel 13:17
text: Then he called his young man that attended upon him, and said, Put now this [woman] out from me, and bolt the door after her.

title: II Samuel 13:18
text: Now she had a vest of many colours upon her; for so were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled. And his attendant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.

title: II Samuel 13:19
text: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her vest of many colours which was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went away, crying out as she went.

title: II Samuel 13:20
text: And Absalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon thy brother been with thee? and now, my sister, be still: he is thy brother; take not this thing to heart. And Tamar remained, and [that] desolate, in her brother Absalom's house.

title: II Samuel 13:21
text: ¶And king David heard of all these things, and he was very angry.

title: II Samuel 13:22
text: And Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had humbled his sister Tamar.

title: II Samuel 13:23
text: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-Hazor, which is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king's sons.

title: II Samuel 13:24
text: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold, now, thy servant has sheepshearers; let the king, I pray thee, and his servants go with thy servant.

title: II Samuel 13:25
text: And the king said to Absalom, No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome to thee. And he urged him, but he would not go; and he blessed him.

title: II Samuel 13:26
text: And Absalom said, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with thee?

title: II Samuel 13:27
text: But Absalom pressed him; and he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

title: II Samuel 13:28
text: And Absalom commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, Smite Amnon; then slay him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.

title: II Samuel 13:29
text: And the servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose, and they rode each upon his mule and fled.

title: II Samuel 13:30
text: ¶And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom has smitten all the king's sons, and there is not one of them left.

title: II Samuel 13:31
text: Then the king arose, and rent his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their garments rent.

title: II Samuel 13:32
text: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men the king's sons; for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he humbled his sister Tamar.

title: II Samuel 13:33
text: And now let not my lord the king take the thing to heart, to say, All the king's sons are dead; for Amnon only is dead.

title: II Samuel 13:34
text: And Absalom fled. And the young man that watched lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, there came much people from the way behind him, from the hill-side.

title: II Samuel 13:35
text: And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the king's sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.

title: II Samuel 13:36
text: And as soon as he had ended speaking, behold, the king's sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept; and the king also and all his servants wept very bitterly.

title: II Samuel 13:37
text: And Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And [David] mourned for his son every day.

title: II Samuel 13:38
text: Now Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

title: II Samuel 13:39
text: And king David longed to go forth to Absalom; for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.

title: II Samuel 14:1
text: ¶And Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

title: II Samuel 14:2
text: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said to her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on mourning garments, I pray, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that hath a long time mourned for the dead;

title: II Samuel 14:3
text: and come to the king, and speak after this manner to him. And Joab put the words into her mouth.

title: II Samuel 14:4
text: And the woman of Tekoah spoke to the king, and she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance, and said, Save, O king!

title: II Samuel 14:5
text: And the king said to her, What aileth thee? And she said, I am indeed a widow woman, and my husband is dead.

title: II Samuel 14:6
text: And thy bondmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other and slew him.

title: II Samuel 14:7
text: And behold, the whole family is risen against thy bondmaid, and they say, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may put him to death, for the life of his brother whom he killed; and we will destroy the heir also: so they will quench my coal which is left, and will not leave to my husband a name or remnant on the earth.

title: II Samuel 14:8
text: And the king said to the woman, Go to thy house, and I will give charge concerning thee.

title: II Samuel 14:9
text: And the woman of Tekoah said to the king, Upon me, my lord, O king, be the iniquity, and upon my father's house; and the king and his throne be guiltless.

title: II Samuel 14:10
text: And the king said, Whoever speaks to thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

title: II Samuel 14:11
text: Then she said, I pray thee, let the king remember Jehovah thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they cut off my son. And he said, [As] Jehovah liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.

title: II Samuel 14:12
text: And the woman said, Let thy bondmaid, I pray thee, speak a word to my lord the king. And he said, Speak.

title: II Samuel 14:13
text: And the woman said, Why then hast thou thought such a thing against God's people? and the king in saying this thing, is as one guilty, in that the king does not bring back his banished one.

title: II Samuel 14:14
text: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; and God has not taken away his life, but devises means that the banished one be not expelled from him.

title: II Samuel 14:15
text: And now that I am come to speak of this thing to my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid; and thy bondmaid said, I will now speak to the king; perhaps the king will perform the request of his handmaid.

title: II Samuel 14:16
text: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

title: II Samuel 14:17
text: And thy bondmaid said, Let the word of my lord the king now be comfortable; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad; and Jehovah thy God will be with thee.

title: II Samuel 14:18
text: And the king answered and said to the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

title: II Samuel 14:19
text: And the king said, Is the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, [As] thy soul liveth, my lord, O king, there is no turning to the right hand or to the left from aught that my lord the king has spoken; for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words into the mouth of thy bondmaid:

title: II Samuel 14:20
text: in order to turn the appearance of the thing has thy servant Joab done this thing; but my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all that is in the earth.

title: II Samuel 14:21
text: ¶And the king said to Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: so go, bring back the young man Absalom.

title: II Samuel 14:22
text: And Joab fell to the ground on his face and bowed himself, and blessed the king; and Joab said, To-day thy servant knows that I have found favour in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king has fulfilled the request of his servant.

title: II Samuel 14:23
text: And Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 14:24
text: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. And Absalom withdrew to his own house, and saw not the king's face.

title: II Samuel 14:25
text: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

title: II Samuel 14:26
text: And when he shaved his head (for it was at every year's end that he shaved it, because it was heavy on him, therefore he shaved it), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.

title: II Samuel 14:27
text: And to Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a beautiful countenance.

title: II Samuel 14:28
text: ¶So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and did not see the king's face.

title: II Samuel 14:29
text: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king; but he would not come to him; and he sent again the second time, but he would not come.

title: II Samuel 14:30
text: Then he said to his servants, See, Joab's allotment is near mine and he has barley there: go and set it on fire. And Absalom's servants set the allotment on fire.

title: II Samuel 14:31
text: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom to [his] house, and said to him, Why have thy servants set my allotment on fire?

title: II Samuel 14:32
text: And Absalom said to Joab, Behold, I sent to thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Why am I come from Geshur? it would have been better for me to be there still. And now let me see the king's face; and if there be iniquity in me, let him slay me.

title: II Samuel 14:33
text: And Joab came to the king, and told him. And he called Absalom, and he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.

title: II Samuel 15:1
text: ¶And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared for himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

title: II Samuel 15:2
text: And Absalom rose early, and stood beside the way of the gate; and it was so, that when any man who had a controversy had to come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.

title: II Samuel 15:3
text: And Absalom said to him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man to hear thee [appointed] by the king.

title: II Samuel 15:4
text: And Absalom said, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who has any controversy and cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!

title: II Samuel 15:5
text: And it was so, that when any man came near to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.

title: II Samuel 15:6
text: And in this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment; and Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

title: II Samuel 15:7
text: ¶And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said to the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay in Hebron my vow which I have vowed to Jehovah.

title: II Samuel 15:8
text: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode in Geshur in Syria, saying, If Jehovah shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve Jehovah.

title: II Samuel 15:9
text: And the king said to him, Go in peace. And he rose up and went to Hebron.

title: II Samuel 15:10
text: And Absalom sent emissaries into all the tribes of Israel, saying, When ye hear the sound of the trumpet, ye shall say, Absalom reigns in Hebron.

title: II Samuel 15:11
text: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were invited; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew nothing.

title: II Samuel 15:12
text: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city, from Giloh, while he offered the sacrifices. And the conspiracy gathered strength; and the people increased continually with Absalom.

title: II Samuel 15:13
text: ¶And there came one to David who reported saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

title: II Samuel 15:14
text: And David said to all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Rise up and let us flee; for we shall not [else] escape from Absalom. Be quick to depart, lest he overtake us quickly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.

title: II Samuel 15:15
text: And the king's servants said to the king, Behold, thy servants [will do] whatever my lord the king shall choose.

title: II Samuel 15:16
text: And the king went forth, and all his household after him, and the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.

title: II Samuel 15:17
text: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and stayed at the remote house.

title: II Samuel 15:18
text: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men that came after him from Gath, passed over before the king.

title: II Samuel 15:19
text: And the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why dost thou also go with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king; for thou art a foreigner, and besides, thou hast emigrated to the place where thou [dwellest].

title: II Samuel 15:20
text: Thou didst come yesterday, and should I this day make thee go up and down with us, seeing I go whither I can? Return and take back thy brethren. Mercy and truth be with thee!

title: II Samuel 15:21
text: And Ittai answered the king and said, [As] Jehovah liveth, and [as] my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.

title: II Samuel 15:22
text: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.

title: II Samuel 15:23
text: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over; the king also himself passed over the torrent Kidron, and all the people passed over, towards the way of the wilderness.

title: II Samuel 15:24
text: ¶And behold, Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had passed completely out of the city.

title: II Samuel 15:25
text: And the king said to Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city. If I shall find favour in the eyes of Jehovah, he will bring me again, and shew me it, and its habitation.

title: II Samuel 15:26
text: But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, [here am] I, let him do to me as seemeth good to him.

title: II Samuel 15:27
text: And the king said to Zadok the priest, Thou art the seer: return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

title: II Samuel 15:28
text: See, I will stop in the plains of the desert, until there come word from you to inform me.

title: II Samuel 15:29
text: And Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem; and they abode there.

title: II Samuel 15:30
text: But David went up by the ascent of the Olives, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot; and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

title: II Samuel 15:31
text: ¶And one told David saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. Then said David, Jehovah, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

title: II Samuel 15:32
text: And it came to pass, when David had come to the summit, where he worshipped God, that behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head.

title: II Samuel 15:33
text: And David said to him, If thou passest on with me, thou wilt be a burden to me;

title: II Samuel 15:34
text: but if thou return to the city, and say to Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father's servant hitherto, so now will I be thy servant; then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.

title: II Samuel 15:35
text: And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? and it shall be, [that] whatsoever thing thou shalt hear out of the king's house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

title: II Samuel 15:36
text: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok's [son], and Jonathan Abiathar's son; and by them ye shall send to me everything that ye shall hear.

title: II Samuel 15:37
text: And Hushai David's friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 16:1
text: ¶And when David was a little past the summit, behold, Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred [loaves] of bread, and a hundred raisin-cakes, and a hundred cakes of summer fruits, and a flask of wine.

title: II Samuel 16:2
text: And the king said to Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses are for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruits for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as are faint in the wilderness may drink.

title: II Samuel 16:3
text: And the king said, And where is thy master's son? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he abides at Jerusalem; for he said, To-day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.

title: II Samuel 16:4
text: And the king said to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained to Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly bow myself: may I find favour in thy sight, my lord, O king.

title: II Samuel 16:5
text: ¶And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, there came out from thence a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed,

title: II Samuel 16:6
text: and cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David; and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

title: II Samuel 16:7
text: And thus said Shimei as he cursed: Away, away, thou man of blood and man of Belial!

title: II Samuel 16:8
text: Jehovah has returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and Jehovah has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son; and behold, thou art [taken] in thine own evil, for thou art a man of blood.

title: II Samuel 16:9
text: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

title: II Samuel 16:10
text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, for Jehovah has said to him, Curse David! Who shall then say, Why dost thou so?

title: II Samuel 16:11
text: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, who came forth of my bowels, seeks my life: how much more now a Benjaminite? let him alone and let him curse; for Jehovah has bidden him.

title: II Samuel 16:12
text: It may be that Jehovah will look on mine affliction, and that Jehovah will requite me good for my being cursed this day.

title: II Samuel 16:13
text: And David and his men went by the way; and Shimei went along on the hill's side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.

title: II Samuel 16:14
text: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.

title: II Samuel 16:15
text: ¶Now Absalom, and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

title: II Samuel 16:16
text: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, Long live the king! Long live the king!

title: II Samuel 16:17
text: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why didst thou not go with thy friend?

title: II Samuel 16:18
text: And Hushai said to Absalom, No; but whom Jehovah, and this people, and all the men of Israel choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.

title: II Samuel 16:19
text: And again, whom should I serve? should it not be in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father's presence, so will I be in thy presence.

title: II Samuel 16:20
text: And Absalom said to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.

title: II Samuel 16:21
text: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to thy father's concubines, whom he has left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art become odious with thy father; and the hands of all that are with thee shall be strong.

title: II Samuel 16:22
text: So they spread a tent for Absalom upon the roof; and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

title: II Samuel 16:23
text: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had inquired of the word of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

title: II Samuel 17:1
text: ¶And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Let me, I pray, choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David to-night;

title: II Samuel 17:2
text: and I will come upon him while he is weary and weak-handed, and will make him afraid; and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only;

title: II Samuel 17:3
text: and I will bring back all the people to thee. The man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: all the people shall be in peace.

title: II Samuel 17:4
text: And the saying was right in the eyes of Absalom, and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

title: II Samuel 17:5
text: And Absalom said, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and we will hear also what he says.

title: II Samuel 17:6
text: And Hushai came to Absalom, and Absalom spoke to him saying, Ahithophel has spoken after this manner: shall we carry out his word? If not, speak thou.

title: II Samuel 17:7
text: And Hushai said to Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good.

title: II Samuel 17:8
text: And Hushai said, Thou knowest thy father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are of exasperated spirit, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field; and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

title: II Samuel 17:9
text: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or some such place; and it will come to pass, when some of them fall at the first, whoever heareth it will say, There has been slaughter among the people that follow Absalom,

title: II Samuel 17:10
text: and even the valiant man whose heart is as the heart of a lion shall utterly melt; for all Israel knows that thy father is a mighty man, and they that are with him are valiant men.

title: II Samuel 17:11
text: But I counsel that all Israel be speedily gathered to thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.

title: II Samuel 17:12
text: And we shall come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falls on the ground; and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.

title: II Samuel 17:13
text: And if he withdraw into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the torrent, until there be not one small stone found there.

title: II Samuel 17:14
text: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. And Jehovah had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, in order that Jehovah might bring evil upon Absalom.

title: II Samuel 17:15
text: ¶And Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.

title: II Samuel 17:16
text: And now send quickly, and tell David saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.

title: II Samuel 17:17
text: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel; and the maid went and told them; and they went and told king David, for they might not be seen to come into the city.

title: II Samuel 17:18
text: But a lad saw them, and told Absalom. Then they went both of them away quickly, and came to the house of a man at Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and they went down there.

title: II Samuel 17:19
text: And the woman took and spread the covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground corn on it; and the thing was not known.

title: II Samuel 17:20
text: And Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house, and said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They have gone over the brook of water. And they sought and could not find [them], and returned to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 17:21
text: And it came to pass after they had departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David; and they said to David, Arise and pass quickly over the water; for thus has Ahithophel counselled against you.

title: II Samuel 17:22
text: ¶Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over the Jordan; by the morning light there was not one of them missing that had not gone over the Jordan.

title: II Samuel 17:23
text: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose and went to his house, to his city, and gave charge to his household, and hanged himself, and he died; and he was buried in the sepulchre of his father.

title: II Samuel 17:24
text: And David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

title: II Samuel 17:25
text: And Absalom set Amasa over the host instead of Joab; which Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Jithra the Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

title: II Samuel 17:26
text: And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.

title: II Samuel 17:27
text: And as soon as David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,

title: II Samuel 17:28
text: brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched [corn], and beans, and lentils, and parched [pulse],

title: II Samuel 17:29
text: and honey, and cream, and sheep, and cheese of kine to David, and to the people that were with him, to eat; for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty in the wilderness.

title: II Samuel 18:1
text: ¶And David marshalled the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

title: II Samuel 18:2
text: And David sent forth the people, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.

title: II Samuel 18:3
text: But the people said, Thou shalt not go forth, for if we should in any case flee, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us; for *thou* art worth ten thousand of us; and now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.

title: II Samuel 18:4
text: And the king said to them, I will do what is good in your sight. And the king stood by the gate-side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

title: II Samuel 18:5
text: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, [Deal] gently for my sake with the young man Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

title: II Samuel 18:6
text: And the people went out into the field against Israel; and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

title: II Samuel 18:7
text: And the people of Israel were routed before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter there that day: twenty thousand men.

title: II Samuel 18:8
text: And the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country; and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

title: II Samuel 18:9
text: ¶And Absalom found himself in the presence of David's servants. And Absalom was riding upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of the great terebinth, and his head caught in the terebinth, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.

title: II Samuel 18:10
text: And a man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in a terebinth.

title: II Samuel 18:11
text: And Joab said to the man that told him, And behold, thou sawest [him], and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten silver pieces and a girdle.

title: II Samuel 18:12
text: And the man said to Joab, Though I should receive a thousand silver pieces in my hand, yet would I not put forth my hand against the king's son; for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Take care, whoever it be [of you], of the young man Absalom.

title: II Samuel 18:13
text: Or I should have acted falsely against mine own life, for there is no matter concealed from the king, and thou wouldest have set thyself against [me].

title: II Samuel 18:14
text: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three spears in his hand, and thrust them into Absalom's body, while he was yet alive in the midst of the terebinth.

title: II Samuel 18:15
text: And ten young men that bore Joab's armour surrounded and smote Absalom, and killed him.

title: II Samuel 18:16
text: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab kept back the people.

title: II Samuel 18:17
text: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and raised a very great heap of stones upon him. And all Israel fled every one to his tent.

title: II Samuel 18:18
text: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a monument, which is in the king's dale; for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance; and he called the monument after his own name; and it is called unto this day, Absalom's memorial.

title: II Samuel 18:19
text: ¶And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, Let me run, I pray, and carry the king the news that Jehovah has avenged him of his enemies.

title: II Samuel 18:20
text: And Joab said to him, Thou shalt not be a bearer of news to-day, but thou shalt carry the news another day; but to-day thou shalt carry no news, because the king's son is dead.

title: II Samuel 18:21
text: Then said Joab to the Cushite, Go, tell the king what thou hast seen. And the Cushite bowed himself to Joab, and ran.

title: II Samuel 18:22
text: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, Come what may, let me, I pray thee, also run after the Cushite. And Joab said, Why wilt thou run, my son, seeing that there is no news suited [to thee]?

title: II Samuel 18:23
text: --But, come what may, let me run. And he said to him, Run. And Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and outstripped the Cushite.

title: II Samuel 18:24
text: And David sat between the two gates; and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate, on to the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man running alone.

title: II Samuel 18:25
text: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is news in his mouth. And he came on and drew near.

title: II Samuel 18:26
text: And the watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the porter and said, Behold a man running alone. And the king said, He also is a bearer of news.

title: II Samuel 18:27
text: And the watchman said, I see the running of the foremost like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man; and comes with good news.

title: II Samuel 18:28
text: And Ahimaaz called and said to the king, Peace! And he fell down to the earth on his face before the king, and said, Blessed be Jehovah thy God, who has delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.

title: II Samuel 18:29
text: And the king said, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz said, I saw a great tumult when Joab sent the king's servant, and me thy servant; but I knew not what it was.

title: II Samuel 18:30
text: And the king said, Turn aside [and] stand here. And he turned aside and stood still.

title: II Samuel 18:31
text: And behold, the Cushite came; and the Cushite said, Let my lord the king receive good tidings, for Jehovah has avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.

title: II Samuel 18:32
text: And the king said to the Cushite, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And the Cushite said, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee for evil, be as that young man.

title: II Samuel 18:33
text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the upper chamber of the gate, and wept; and as he went, he said thus: O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died in thy stead, O Absalom, my son, my son!

title: II Samuel 19:1
text: ¶And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.

title: II Samuel 19:2
text: And the victory that day was [turned] into mourning for all the people; for the people heard say that day, The king is grieved for his son.

title: II Samuel 19:3
text: And the people stole away that day into the city, as people steal away when ashamed of fleeing in battle.

title: II Samuel 19:4
text: And the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!

title: II Samuel 19:5
text: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast put to shame this day the faces of all thy servants who have this day saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives and the lives of thy concubines;

title: II Samuel 19:6
text: in that thou lovest them that hate thee, and hatest those that love thee. For thou hast declared this day, that neither princes nor servants are anything to thee: for to-day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died to-day, then it would have been right in thine eyes.

title: II Samuel 19:7
text: But now arise, go forth, and speak consolingly to thy servants; for I swear by Jehovah, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night; and that would be worse to thee than all the evil that has befallen thee from thy youth until now.

title: II Samuel 19:8
text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, Behold, the king is sitting in the gate. And all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his tent.

title: II Samuel 19:9
text: ¶And all the people were at strife throughout the tribes of Israel, saying, The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land because of Absalom.

title: II Samuel 19:10
text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle; and now why are ye silent as to bringing the king back?

title: II Samuel 19:11
text: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Judah saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, to his house.

title: II Samuel 19:12
text: Ye are my brethren, ye are my bone and my flesh; and why will ye be the last to bring back the king?

title: II Samuel 19:13
text: And say to Amasa, Art thou not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually instead of Joab.

title: II Samuel 19:14
text: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah as of one man; and they sent to the king, Return, thou and all thy servants.

title: II Samuel 19:15
text: And the king returned and came as far as the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over the Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:16
text: ¶And Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjaminite, who was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

title: II Samuel 19:17
text: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they forded the Jordan before the king.

title: II Samuel 19:18
text: And a ferry boat passed to and fro to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king as he was [just] crossing over the Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:19
text: And he said to the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity to me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to heart.

title: II Samuel 19:20
text: For thy servant knows that I have sinned; and behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.

title: II Samuel 19:21
text: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Should not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed Jehovah's anointed?

title: II Samuel 19:22
text: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries to me? Should there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?

title: II Samuel 19:23
text: And the king said to Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king swore to him.

title: II Samuel 19:24
text: ¶And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. Now he had neither washed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came [again] in peace.

title: II Samuel 19:25
text: And as soon as Jerusalem came to meet the king, the king said to him, Why didst thou not go with me, Mephibosheth?

title: II Samuel 19:26
text: And he said, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me; for thy servant said, I will saddle me the ass, and ride thereon, and go with the king; for thy servant is lame.

title: II Samuel 19:27
text: And he has slandered thy servant to my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God; do therefore what is good in thy sight.

title: II Samuel 19:28
text: For all my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king; and thou didst set thy servant among them that eat at thine own table. What further right therefore have I? and for what should I cry any more to the king?

title: II Samuel 19:29
text: And the king said to him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.

title: II Samuel 19:30
text: And Mephibosheth said to the king, Let him even take all, since my lord the king is come again in peace to his own house.

title: II Samuel 19:31
text: ¶And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over the Jordan with the king, to conduct him over the Jordan.

title: II Samuel 19:32
text: And Barzillai was very aged, eighty years old; and it was he that had maintained the king while he abode at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.

title: II Samuel 19:33
text: And the king said to Barzillai, Pass thou over with me, and I will maintain thee with me in Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 19:34
text: And Barzillai said to the king, How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

title: II Samuel 19:35
text: I am this day eighty years old: can I discern between good and bad? can thy servant taste what I eat and what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? and why should thy servant be yet a burden to my lord the king?

title: II Samuel 19:36
text: Thy servant will go a little way over the Jordan with the king; and why should the king recompense it to me with this reward?

title: II Samuel 19:37
text: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham: let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what seems good to thee.

title: II Samuel 19:38
text: And the king said, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which seems good to thee; and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.

title: II Samuel 19:39
text: And all the people went over the Jordan; and the king went over; and the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned to his own place.

title: II Samuel 19:40
text: ¶And the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him; and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.

title: II Samuel 19:41
text: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David's men with him, over the Jordan?

title: II Samuel 19:42
text: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to me; and why then are ye angry for this matter? have we eaten anything which came from the king, or has he given us any present?

title: II Samuel 19:43
text: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, I have ten parts in the king and I have also more right in David than thou; and why didst thou slight me? and was not my advice the first, to bring back my king? And the words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel.

title: II Samuel 20:1
text: ¶And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite; and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, Israel.

title: II Samuel 20:2
text: Then all the men of Israel went up from after David, following Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah clave to their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 20:3
text: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women, concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house of confinement and maintained them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.

title: II Samuel 20:4
text: ¶And the king said to Amasa, Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and do thou attend here.

title: II Samuel 20:5
text: So Amasa went to call together [the men of] Judah; but he delayed longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

title: II Samuel 20:6
text: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom. Take thou thy lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fortified cities and escape our sight.

title: II Samuel 20:7
text: And there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: II Samuel 20:8
text: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came before them. And Joab was girded with his coat, his dress, and upon it was the girdle of the sword which was fastened on his loins in its sheath; and as he went forth it fell out.

title: II Samuel 20:9
text: And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou well, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.

title: II Samuel 20:10
text: And Amasa had taken no notice of the sword that was in Joab's hand: so he smote him with it in the belly and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

title: II Samuel 20:11
text: And one of Joab's young men stood by [Amasa] and said, He that favours Joab, and he that is for David, let him follow Joab.

title: II Samuel 20:12
text: Now Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by stood still.

title: II Samuel 20:13
text: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri,

title: II Samuel 20:14
text: ¶who went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth-Maacah, and all the Berim; and they gathered together, and went also after him.

title: II Samuel 20:15
text: And they came and besieged him in Abel-Beth-Maacah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it was raised in the trench; and all the people that were with Joab sapped the wall, to throw it down.

title: II Samuel 20:16
text: And a wise woman cried out of the city, Hear, hear: say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.

title: II Samuel 20:17
text: And he came near to her; and the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he said, I [am he]. And she said to him, Listen to the words of thy handmaid. And he said, I am listening.

title: II Samuel 20:18
text: And she spoke saying, They were wont to speak in old time saying, Just inquire in Abel; and so they ended.

title: II Samuel 20:19
text: I am peaceable [and] faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of Jehovah?

title: II Samuel 20:20
text: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

title: II Samuel 20:21
text: The matter is not so; but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David: give up him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

title: II Samuel 20:22
text: Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

title: II Samuel 20:23
text: ¶And Joab was over all the host of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;

title: II Samuel 20:24
text: and Adoram was over the levy; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;

title: II Samuel 20:25
text: and Sheva was scribe; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

title: II Samuel 20:26
text: and Ira also, the Jairite, was David's chief ruler.

title: II Samuel 21:1
text: ¶And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David inquired of Jehovah. And Jehovah said, It is for Saul, and for [his] house of blood, because he slew the Gibeonites.

title: II Samuel 21:2
text: And the king called the Gibeonites, and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remainder of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn to them; and Saul sought to smite them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.)

title: II Samuel 21:3
text: And David said to the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and with what shall I make atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of Jehovah?

title: II Samuel 21:4
text: And the Gibeonites said to him, As to Saul and his house, it is with us no question of receiving silver or gold, neither is it for us to have any man put to death in Israel. And he said, What ye say will I do for you.

title: II Samuel 21:5
text: And they said to the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in all the borders of Israel,

title: II Samuel 21:6
text: let seven men of his sons be given up to us, and we will hang them up to Jehovah in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Jehovah. And the king said, I will give [them].

title: II Samuel 21:7
text: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Jehovah's oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

title: II Samuel 21:8
text: And the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of [the sister of] Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite;

title: II Samuel 21:9
text: and he gave them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before Jehovah. And they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the first days of the harvest, in the beginning of barley harvest.

title: II Samuel 21:10
text: ¶Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured on them out of the heavens, and suffered neither the fowl of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

title: II Samuel 21:11
text: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

title: II Samuel 21:12
text: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the open place of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, the day the Philistines had smitten Saul in Gilboa;

title: II Samuel 21:13
text: and he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

title: II Samuel 21:14
text: And they buried [them] with the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the sepulchre of Kish his father; and they did all that the king had commanded. And afterwards God was propitious to the land.

title: II Samuel 21:15
text: ¶And the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought with the Philistines. And David was exhausted.

title: II Samuel 21:16
text: And Ishbibenob, who was of the children of Raphah--the weight of his lance was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with new [armour] --thought to smite David.

title: II Samuel 21:17
text: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.

title: II Samuel 21:18
text: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines, at Gob; then Sibbechai the Hushathite smote Saph, who was of the children of Raphah.

title: II Samuel 21:19
text: And there was again a battle at Gob with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, smote Goliath the Gittite; now the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam.

title: II Samuel 21:20
text: And there was again a battle, at Gath; and there was a man [there] of great stature, that had on each hand six fingers, and on each foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to Raphah.

title: II Samuel 21:21
text: And he defied Israel; but Jonathan the son of Shimea David's brother smote him.

title: II Samuel 21:22
text: These four were born to Raphah, in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

title: II Samuel 22:1
text: ¶And David spoke to Jehovah the words of this song in the day that Jehovah had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul.

title: II Samuel 22:2
text: ¶And he said, Jehovah is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;

title: II Samuel 22:3
text: God is my rock, in him will I trust--My shield, and the horn of my salvation, My high tower, and my refuge, My saviour: thou wilt save me from violence.

title: II Samuel 22:4
text: I will call upon Jehovah, who is to be praised; So shall I be saved from mine enemies.

title: II Samuel 22:5
text: For the waves of death encompassed me, Torrents of Belial made me afraid.

title: II Samuel 22:6
text: The bands of Sheol surrounded me; The cords of death encountered me;

title: II Samuel 22:7
text: In my distress I called upon Jehovah, And I cried to my God; And he heard my voice out of his temple, And my cry [came] into his ears.

title: II Samuel 22:8
text: Then the earth shook, and quaked; The foundations of the heavens trembled And shook because he was wroth.

title: II Samuel 22:9
text: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, And fire out of his mouth devoured: Coals burned forth from it.

title: II Samuel 22:10
text: And he bowed the heavens, and came down; And darkness was under his feet.

title: II Samuel 22:11
text: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly; And he was seen upon the wings of the wind.

title: II Samuel 22:12
text: And he made darkness round about him a tent, Gatherings of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

title: II Samuel 22:13
text: From the brightness before him Burned forth coals of fire.

title: II Samuel 22:14
text: Jehovah thundered from the heavens, And the Most High uttered his voice.

title: II Samuel 22:15
text: And he sent arrows, and scattered [mine enemies]; Lightning, and discomfited them.

title: II Samuel 22:16
text: And the beds of the sea were seen, The foundations of the world were uncovered At the rebuke of Jehovah, At the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

title: II Samuel 22:17
text: He reached forth from above, he took me, He drew me out of great waters;

title: II Samuel 22:18
text: He delivered me from my strong enemy, From them that hated me; For they were mightier than I.

title: II Samuel 22:19
text: They encountered me in the day of my calamity; But Jehovah was my stay.

title: II Samuel 22:20
text: And he brought me forth into a large place; He delivered me, because he delighted in me.

title: II Samuel 22:21
text: Jehovah hath rewarded me according to my righteousness, According to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.

title: II Samuel 22:22
text: For I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And have not wickedly departed from my God.

title: II Samuel 22:23
text: For all his ordinances were before me, And his statutes, I did not depart from them,

title: II Samuel 22:24
text: And I was upright before him, And kept myself from mine iniquity.

title: II Samuel 22:25
text: And Jehovah hath recompensed me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his sight.

title: II Samuel 22:26
text: With the gracious thou dost shew thyself gracious; With the upright man thou dost shew thyself upright;

title: II Samuel 22:27
text: With the pure thou dost shew thyself pure; And with the perverse thou dost shew thyself contrary.

title: II Samuel 22:28
text: And the afflicted people thou dost save; And thine eyes are upon the haughty, [whom] thou bringest down.

title: II Samuel 22:29
text: For thou art my lamp, Jehovah; And Jehovah enlighteneth my darkness.

title: II Samuel 22:30
text: For by thee I have run through a troop; By my God have I leaped over a wall.

title: II Samuel 22:31
text: As for *God, his way is perfect; The word of Jehovah is tried: He is a shield to all that trust in him.

title: II Samuel 22:32
text: For who is *God, save Jehovah? And who is a rock, save our God?

title: II Samuel 22:33
text: *God is my strong fortress, And he maketh my way perfectly smooth.

title: II Samuel 22:34
text: He maketh my feet like hinds' [feet], And setteth me upon my high places.

title: II Samuel 22:35
text: He teacheth my hands to war, And mine arms bend a bow of brass.

title: II Samuel 22:36
text: And thou didst give me the shield of thy salvation, And thy condescending gentleness hath made me great.

title: II Samuel 22:37
text: Thou enlargedst my steps under me; And mine ankles did not slip.

title: II Samuel 22:38
text: I pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them, And I turned not again till they were consumed.

title: II Samuel 22:39
text: And I have consumed them and have crushed them, and they rose not again; Yea, they fell under my feet.

title: II Samuel 22:40
text: And thou girdedst me with strength to battle: Thou didst subdue under me those that rose up against me.

title: II Samuel 22:41
text: And mine enemies didst thou make to turn their backs unto me, And those that hated me I destroyed.

title: II Samuel 22:42
text: They looked, and there was none to save--Unto Jehovah, and he answered them not.

title: II Samuel 22:43
text: And I did beat them small as the dust of the earth, I trod them as the mire of the streets; I stamped upon them.

title: II Samuel 22:44
text: And thou hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, Thou hast kept me to be head of the nations: A people I knew not doth serve me:

title: II Samuel 22:45
text: Strangers come cringing unto me: At the hearing of the ear, they obey me.

title: II Samuel 22:46
text: Strangers have faded away, And they come trembling forth from their close places.

title: II Samuel 22:47
text: Jehovah liveth; and blessed be my rock; And exalted be the God, the rock of my salvation,

title: II Samuel 22:48
text: The *God who hath avenged me, And hath brought the peoples under me.

title: II Samuel 22:49
text: He brought me forth from mine enemies: Yea, thou hast lifted me up above them that rose up against me; From the man of violence hast thou delivered me.

title: II Samuel 22:50
text: Therefore will I give thanks to thee, Jehovah, among the nations, And will sing psalms to thy name.

title: II Samuel 22:51
text: [It is he] who giveth great deliverances to his king, And sheweth loving-kindness to his anointed, To David, and to his seed for evermore.

title: II Samuel 23:1
text: ¶Now these are the last words of David: David the son of Jesse saith, And the man who was raised up on high, The anointed of the God of Jacob, And the sweet psalmist of Israel saith,

title: II Samuel 23:2
text: The Spirit of Jehovah spoke by me, And his word was on my tongue.

title: II Samuel 23:3
text: The God of Israel said, The Rock of Israel spoke to me, The ruler among men shall be just, Ruling in the fear of God;

title: II Samuel 23:4
text: And [he shall be] as the light of the morning, [like] the rising of the sun, A morning without clouds; [When] from the sunshine, after rain, The green grass springeth from the earth.

title: II Samuel 23:5
text: Although my house be not so before *God, Yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, Ordered in every way and sure; For [this is] all my salvation, and every desire, Although he make [it] not to grow.

title: II Samuel 23:6
text: But [the sons] of Belial [are] all of them as thorns thrust away, Because they cannot be taken with hands;

title: II Samuel 23:7
text: And the man that will touch them provideth himself with iron and the staff of a spear; And they shall be utterly burned with fire in [their] place.

title: II Samuel 23:8
text: ¶These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: Joseb-Bassebeth, Tachkemonite the chief of the captains: he was Adino the Eznite; he [fought] against eight hundred, slain [by him] at one time.

title: II Samuel 23:9
text: And after him, Eleazar the son of Dodo the son of an Ahohite: he was one of the three mighty men with David, when they had defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone up.

title: II Samuel 23:10
text: He arose and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave to the sword; and Jehovah wrought a great deliverance that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.

title: II Samuel 23:11
text: And after him, Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite: the Philistines were gathered into a troop, and there was there a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people had fled before the Philistines;

title: II Samuel 23:12
text: and he stood in the midst of the plot and delivered it, and smote the Philistines, and Jehovah wrought a great deliverance.

title: II Samuel 23:13
text: And three of the thirty chiefs went down, and came to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam, when the troop of the Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.

title: II Samuel 23:14
text: And David was then in the stronghold; and the Philistines' garrison was then at Bethlehem.

title: II Samuel 23:15
text: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me to drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, which is in the gate!

title: II Samuel 23:16
text: And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, which is in the gate, and took it, and brought it to David; however he would not drink of it, but poured it out to Jehovah.

title: II Samuel 23:17
text: And he said, Be it far from me, Jehovah, that I should do this thing! is it not the blood of the men that went at the risk of their lives? Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.

title: II Samuel 23:18
text: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was the chief of three; and he brandished his spear against three hundred and slew them; and he had a name among the three.

title: II Samuel 23:19
text: Was he not most honourable of three? and he was their captain; but he did not attain to the [first] three.

title: II Samuel 23:20
text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man, great in exploits, of Kabzeel: he it was that smote two lions of Moab; and he went down and smote a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.

title: II Samuel 23:21
text: He also smote the Egyptian, an imposing man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.

title: II Samuel 23:22
text: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and he had a name among the three mighty men.

title: II Samuel 23:23
text: He was honoured above the thirty, but he did not attain to the [first] three. And David set him in his council.

title: II Samuel 23:24
text: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

title: II Samuel 23:25
text: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

title: II Samuel 23:26
text: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,

title: II Samuel 23:27
text: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,

title: II Samuel 23:28
text: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,

title: II Samuel 23:29
text: Heleb the son of Baanah, the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,

title: II Samuel 23:30
text: Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash,

title: II Samuel 23:31
text: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,

title: II Samuel 23:32
text: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, of the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,

title: II Samuel 23:33
text: Shammah the Ararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,

title: II Samuel 23:34
text: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maachathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

title: II Samuel 23:35
text: Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

title: II Samuel 23:36
text: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,

title: II Samuel 23:37
text: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armour-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,

title: II Samuel 23:38
text: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

title: II Samuel 23:39
text: Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.

title: II Samuel 24:1
text: ¶And again the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.

title: II Samuel 24:2
text: And the king said to Joab the captain of the host, who was with him, Go, I pray thee, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and count the people, that I may know the number of the people.

title: II Samuel 24:3
text: And Joab said to the king, May Jehovah thy God even add to the people, how many soever they be, a hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see [it]; but why does my lord the king delight in this thing?

title: II Samuel 24:4
text: But the king's word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the army. And Joab and the captains of the army went out from the presence of the king to count the people of Israel.

title: II Samuel 24:5
text: And they passed over the Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the midst of the ravine of Gad, and toward Jaazer.

title: II Samuel 24:6
text: And they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and came to Dan-jaan, and to the environs of Sidon;

title: II Samuel 24:7
text: and they came to the fortified city of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites and of the Canaanites; and went out to the south of Judah, to Beer-sheba.

title: II Samuel 24:8
text: And they went through all the land, and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

title: II Samuel 24:9
text: And Joab gave the sum of the number of the people to the king; and there were of Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

title: II Samuel 24:10
text: ¶And David's heart smote him after he had numbered the people. And David said to Jehovah, I have sinned greatly in what I have done; and now, I beseech thee, Jehovah, put away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

title: II Samuel 24:11
text: And when David arose in the morning, the word of Jehovah came to the prophet Gad, David's seer, saying,

title: II Samuel 24:12
text: Go and say to David, Thus saith Jehovah: I impose on thee three [things]; choose one of them that I may do it unto thee.

title: II Samuel 24:13
text: And Gad came to David, and told him, and said to him, Shall seven years of famine come to thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine adversaries while they pursue thee? or shall there be three days' pestilence in thy land? Now be aware and consider what word I shall bring again to him that sent me.

title: II Samuel 24:14
text: And David said to Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall, I pray thee, into the hand of Jehovah; for his mercies are great; but let me not fall into the hand of man.

title: II Samuel 24:15
text: And Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the set time; and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.

title: II Samuel 24:16
text: And the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it; but Jehovah repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed among the people, It is enough: withdraw now thine hand. And the angel of Jehovah was by the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

title: II Samuel 24:17
text: And David spoke to Jehovah when he saw the angel that smote among the people, and said, Behold, it is I that have sinned, and it is I that have committed iniquity; but these sheep, what have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, be on me, and on my father's house!

title: II Samuel 24:18
text: ¶And Gad came that day to David, and said to him, Go up, rear an altar to Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

title: II Samuel 24:19
text: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as Jehovah had commanded.

title: II Samuel 24:20
text: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on towards him; and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.

title: II Samuel 24:21
text: And Araunah said, Why is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing-floor of thee, to build an altar to Jehovah, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

title: II Samuel 24:22
text: And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer up that which is good in his sight: see, [here are] oxen for the burnt-offering, and the threshing-sledges and implements of the oxen for wood.

title: II Samuel 24:23
text: All these things, O king, doth Araunah give to the king. And Araunah said to the king, Jehovah thy God accept thee.

title: II Samuel 24:24
text: And the king said to Araunah, No; but I will in any case buy [them] of thee at a price: neither will I offer up to Jehovah my God burnt-offerings without cost. And David bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

title: II Samuel 24:25
text: And David built there an altar to Jehovah, and offered up burnt-offerings and peace-offerings. And Jehovah was propitious to the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

title: I Kings 1:1
text: ¶And king David was old [and] advanced in age; and they covered him with clothes, but he obtained no warmth.

title: I Kings 1:2
text: And his servants said to him, Let there be found for my lord the king a young virgin; and let her stand before the king, and let her cherish him, and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get warm.

title: I Kings 1:3
text: And they sought for a fair damsel throughout the territory of Israel, and found Abishag a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

title: I Kings 1:4
text: And the damsel was very fair; and cherished the king, and ministered to him; but the king knew her not.

title: I Kings 1:5
text: ¶And Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king; and he provided himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

title: I Kings 1:6
text: And his father had not grieved him at any time in saying, Why doest thou so? and he was also a very comely man; and [his mother] bore him after Absalom.

title: I Kings 1:7
text: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest; and they helped Adonijah and followed [him].

title: I Kings 1:8
text: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men whom David had, were not with Adonijah.

title: I Kings 1:9
text: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and oxen and fatted cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which is by En-rogel, and invited all his brethren, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants;

title: I Kings 1:10
text: but Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he did not invite.

title: I Kings 1:11
text: ¶And Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith is king, and David our lord does not know [it]?

title: I Kings 1:12
text: And now, come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

title: I Kings 1:13
text: Go and get thee in to king David, and say to him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, swear to thy handmaid saying, Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne? why then does Adonijah reign?

title: I Kings 1:14
text: Behold, while thou yet talkest there with the king, I also will come in after thee and confirm thy words.

title: I Kings 1:15
text: And Bathsheba went in to the king into the chamber; and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite ministered to the king.

title: I Kings 1:16
text: And Bathsheba bowed and did obeisance to the king. And the king said, What wouldest thou?

title: I Kings 1:17
